clue.text: Line on map is alternative motorway

parts.note: an alternative choice is the other one
M is the standard abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: A mapmaker marks a new motorway as an alternative route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line on map' looks like a road, but it is a weather-map line, and the motorway gives only its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An isotherm is a line on a weather map joining places of equal temperature.

clue.text: I'm not one to weaken

parts.note: taken as written without its apostrophe
not one but two is a pair

explanation.surface: A modest speaker insists they are not the type to give in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not one' reads as a denial, but means two.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair is to damage or lessen the strength of something.

clue.text: Do they fruit where all else dies?

definitions.text: Do they fruit where all else dies?

parts.words: Do they fruit where all else dies?
parts.note: describes Mediterranean trees that crop on dry, stony ground where little else survives, with a play on nothing living

explanation.surface: A question about hardy plants that bear fruit in barren land.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive trees are famously hardy, cropping in poor, arid soil.

clue.text: Hound is a worrier

explanation.surface: A dog is prone to anxiety.
explanation.definitionFit: A harrier is a dog bred for hunting hares, and also one who harries or harasses.

clue.text: Support for the others

explanation.surface: A prop is provided for everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: A rest is a prop or stand, and the rest means the remaining people or things.

clue.text: Made boring speech-it wasn't in verse

explanation.surface: Someone droned on, and at least it wasn't poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: To prose is to talk tediously at length; a text so treated was rendered in prose, the opposite of verse.

clue.text: Nastier sort of wine?

indicators.note: sort of signals that the letters of nastier are sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: A rude question about a resinated drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Cops' raid may be irregular

indicators.note: may be suggests these letters could become something else, rearranged

explanation.surface: A police raid might be against the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Sporadic means occurring at irregular intervals, now and then.

clue.text: Donning gear and coming into line

explanation.surface: Soldiers put on kit and fall in.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressing is putting clothes on, and in drill, dressing ranks is aligning troops in a straight row.

clue.text: Decorous pink and yellow bloomer

parts.note: decorous means proper and prim
rose is a shade of pink

explanation.surface: A prim lady in pink and yellow takes a tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a blunder or old-fashioned knickers, but here it is simply a plant that blooms, a pale yellow spring flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The primrose is a wild plant with pale yellow flowers in spring.

clue.text: Did one's best to get right inside the kiln

indicators.note: inside tells us the letter for right goes into the word for the kiln

parts.note: a stove is a heated drying room or kiln

explanation.surface: A potter tried hard to get the firing right in the kiln.
explanation.definitionFit: Strove is the past tense of strive, to make every effort.

clue.text: Soldiers to a certain extent repay in kind

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of soldiers
quite means fairly, to some degree

explanation.surface: Troops partly pay back what they owe.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: To requite is to return a favour or injury with the same.

clue.text: Peninsular where one has to live beside drowned valley

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to be is to exist, to live
a ria is a long inlet formed when the sea floods a river valley

explanation.surface: Somebody must settle beside a flooded valley on a peninsula.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'Peninsular', an adjective; the definition needs the noun 'peninsula', a slip of one letter, with 'where' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Iberia is the peninsula in south-west Europe shared by Spain and Portugal.

clue.text: Room in their beaks for about fifty-one nuts?

definitions.text: Room in their beaks for about fifty-one nuts?

indicators.note: about tells us the nuts go round the number fifty-one

parts.note: pecans are a kind of nut
LI is fifty-one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Some birds have pouched bills big enough to carry around fifty-one nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: these birds really do carry food in their huge stretchy bill pouches.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelicans are large water birds whose bills carry a stretchy pouch that holds a great deal.

clue.text: Standard method of salute

parts.note: reads as a usual way to salute, but the standard is a flag, lowered briefly as a mark of respect

explanation.surface: A question of the normal way to salute.
explanation.definitionFit: Dipping a flag means lowering it briefly and raising it again as a salute.

clue.text: Ritual action bedevilled by straight speaking

indicators.note: bedevilled means thrown into confusion, so the letters of ritual action are jumbled

explanation.surface: A religious ceremony is spoiled by someone talking bluntly.
explanation.definitionFit: Articulation is clear, distinct speech, saying words plainly.

clue.text: In order to ridicule, tipping the lady out of bed, for example?

definitions.text: tipping the lady out of bed, for example

explanation.surface: A prank of upending a woman from her bed invites mockery.
explanation.definitionFit: A fair game is a legitimate target for mockery; whimsically, a game played on a fair woman, the fair being an old term for a lady.

clue.text: County town employees taking the ring road

parts.note: a firm's employees are its staff
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Council workers head for the ring road out of town.
explanation.walkthrough: STAFFORD is the county town of Staffordshire, in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Stafford is the administrative centre of Staffordshire, its county town.

clue.text: I can point it out, being ready beforehand

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters of the fodder are rearranged

parts.note: the clue's own words I CAN POINT IT, which with the missing A give the twelve letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone offers to show where something is, being well prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the anagram signal, but I CAN POINT IT is one A short of the answer's twelve letters, so the clue as printed (or its setter) has lost an A.
explanation.definitionFit: Anticipation is foresight: expecting and preparing for something before it arrives.

clue.text: Many hurry to hand out punishment

parts.note: C, the Roman numeral for a hundred, stands for many
to hasten is to hurry

explanation.surface: Many people rush to dish out penalties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' gives only the letter C, a hundred in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: To chasten is to discipline or correct someone by punishing them.

clue.text: it's best to settle for one parent

parts.note: to opt for is to choose or settle for
I is the Roman numeral for one
mum is a mother, a parent

explanation.surface: Advice to make do with a single parent.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimum means most favourable, the finest possible.

clue.text: Viewpoint from street can stagger everyone.

annotationWithheld.why: Viewpoint from street can stagger everyone. — ST plus an anagram of CAN gives STANC; no recognised abbreviation turns 'everyone' into the final E, so a word seems misprinted or missing
annotationWithheld.clue: Viewpoint from street can stagger everyone.

clue.text: Virginal, but has followers, 'one hears

indicators.note: one hears signals we want the sound of the word, not its spelling

parts.note: someone with followers is chased

explanation.surface: A pure maiden finds herself pursued.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means pure, abstaining from sex.

clue.text: Stops judge joining gunmen in school

parts.note: a referee, or ref, judges a match
RA is the Royal Artillery, the army's gunners
taken as written

explanation.surface: A judge teams up with armed men at a school to halt something.
explanation.walkthrough: RA is the Royal Artillery, the British Army's gunners.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain is to hold back or desist from doing something.

clue.text: Good man has urge to join up

parts.note: ST, for saint, is the crossword's good man
an itch is a restless urge

explanation.surface: A virtuous man is keen to enlist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'join up' suggests enlisting, but it means sew together.
explanation.definitionFit: To stitch is to sew pieces together with thread.

clue.text: A party loses heart, given shock therapy

indicators.note: heart signals the central letter of the word loses

parts.note: ECT is electroconvulsive therapy, a shock treatment

explanation.surface: A political party loses its nerve and is sent for electric shock treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses heart' sounds like despair, but means the heart of the word 'loses', its middle letter S.
explanation.definitionFit: A sect is a faction or party, especially a breakaway group.

clue.text: Animal making an attempt to turn it round

parts.note: to have a go is to make an attempt, so an attempt is a go
U stands for a turn, as in a U-turn

indicators.note: round means the word it is turned the other way

explanation.surface: Something tries to turn an object round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' gives U from the U-turn, and 'round' turns IT backwards to TI.
explanation.definitionFit: The agouti is a long-legged rodent of Central and South America.

clue.text: 28 across, with a period of time in America

parts.note: a term is a fixed period, as a school term
taken as written
US is the United States

explanation.surface: A school term spent in the United States finishes things off.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the solution to 28 across.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminus is the final point of something, the place where a line stops.

clue.text: Measure excessive noise and force closure

parts.note: an en is a printer's measure of width
a din is a loud noise
G is the symbol for the force of gravity, as in g-force

explanation.surface: Someone gauges a racket and forces it to shut down.
explanation.walkthrough: EN is a printing measure, half an em.
explanation.definitionFit: An ending is a conclusion, the point at which something is finished.

clue.text: Crazed pets made mad dash

indicators.note: crazed means driven wild, so the letters of pets made are jumbled

explanation.surface: Frenzied pets break into a frantic run.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a sudden panicked rush of animals or people.
